title: Periodic quarter-wave Bragg stack centered at 550 nm for visible reflection
scientific_hypothesis: A periodic quarter-wave stack with 15 HfO2/SiO2 pairs centered at 550 nm will achieve high reflectance across 400-700 nm while maintaining high transmittance at 1530-1565 nm, with performance improving as layer thicknesses are tuned from the ideal quarter-wave condition.
design_principle: Quarter-wave Bragg reflectors create a photonic stopband centered at the design wavelength. By centering the stopband at 550 nm (middle of 400-700 nm), the 1530-1565 nm band falls well outside the stopband and should transmit. The HfO2/SiO2 index contrast provides sufficient reflectivity per interface.
proposed_topology: Air | (hfo2, sio2) repeated 15 times | sio2 substrate, total 30 layers
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 30 layers, initialized near quarter-wave at 550 nm
manufacturing_considerations: 30 layers is within typical ion-beam sputtering capability
HfO2/SiO2 is a standard low-stress pair for space optics
quarter-wave thicknesses are manufacturable with standard monitoring
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method for multilayer interference
HfO2/SiO2 dispersion data from measured datasets
expected_advantages: High index contrast yields strong reflection per pair
known_risks: Fixed period may not cover full 400-700 nm band evenly
Edge wavelengths (400 nm, 700 nm) may have lower reflectance
30 layers may accumulate stress or absorption losses
execution_request_english: Design a 30-layer periodic multilayer coating on SiO2 (Lemarchand) substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence: alternating hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) layers, starting with hfo2, repeated 15 times for 30 total layers. Optimize individual layer thicknesses to maximize transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band and reflectance in 400-700 nm band. Initialize thicknesses near quarter-wave condition at 550 nm center wavelength. Use measured refractive index data for hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) from the material catalog. Total layer count fixed at 30.
